subject: Biology
title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
summary: The flower is the site of sexual reproduction. The stamen's anther makes pollen grains (male gametophytes) by microsporogenesis; the ovule makes the embryo sac (female gametophyte) by megasporogenesis.
Pollination brings pollen to the stigma — by wind, water or animals. Plants have outbreeding devices to avoid self-pollination; pollen–pistil interaction decides compatibility.
Angiosperms show double fertilisation: one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy → zygote) and the other with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion → primary endosperm nucleus, 3n).
After fertilisation the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary the fruit. Special cases: apomixis, polyembryony and parthenocarpy.

formulas.name: Anther structure
formulas.formula: bilobed, dithecous, tetrasporangiate;  wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, tapetum (nourishes pollen; dense cytoplasm, often more than one nucleus)

formulas.name: Microsporogenesis
formulas.formula: microspore mother cell (2n) → meiosis → microspore tetrad (n) → pollen grains

formulas.name: Pollen grain
formulas.formula: exine of sporopollenin (most resistant organic material known; germ pores where absent) + intine (cellulose, pectin);  mature pollen: vegetative cell (large) + generative cell (small, divides into 2 male gametes)
formulas.note: In over 60% of angiosperms pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage.

formulas.name: Ovule parts
formulas.formula: funicle, hilum, integuments, micropyle, chalaza, nucellus, embryo sac

formulas.name: Megasporogenesis and embryo sac
formulas.formula: megaspore mother cell → meiosis → 4 megaspores (one functional) → 3 mitotic divisions → 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac (monosporic, Polygonum type)

formulas.name: Embryo sac cells
formulas.formula: micropylar: egg apparatus (egg + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus);  centre: central cell with 2 polar nuclei;  chalazal: 3 antipodals

formulas.name: Types of pollination
formulas.formula: autogamy (same flower);  geitonogamy (another flower, same plant — genetically like autogamy);  xenogamy (different plant — genetically different pollen)
formulas.note: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination (needs an agent) but genetically self-pollination.

formulas.name: Chasmogamous vs cleistogamous
formulas.formula: chasmogamous: open flowers;  cleistogamous: never open, assured seed-set without pollinators (Viola, Oxalis, Commelina)

formulas.name: Pollinating agents
formulas.formula: wind (light non-sticky pollen, feathery stigma, one ovule — grasses, maize tassels);  water (Vallisneria, Hydrilla, Zostera — water hyacinth and water lily are insect/wind pollinated);  insects (large colourful, fragrant flowers, nectar)

formulas.name: Outbreeding devices
formulas.formula: pollen release and stigma receptivity not synchronised;  anther and stigma at different positions;  self-incompatibility;  unisexual flowers (castor, maize — prevents autogamy; papaya dioecious — prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy)

formulas.name: Double fertilisation
formulas.formula: syngamy: male gamete + egg → zygote (2n);  triple fusion: male gamete + 2 polar nuclei → PEN (3n)

formulas.name: Post-fertilisation changes
formulas.formula: ovule → seed;  integuments → seed coat;  ovary → fruit;  ovary wall → pericarp;  zygote → embryo;  PEN → endosperm

formulas.name: Endosperm types
formulas.formula: free-nuclear (coconut water: thousands of free nuclei);  cellular (white kernel of coconut);  albuminous seeds keep endosperm (wheat, maize, castor);  non-albuminous use it up (pea, groundnut, bean)

formulas.name: Apomixis and polyembryony
formulas.formula: apomixis: seed without fertilisation (Asteraceae, grasses) — preserves hybrid characters;  polyembryony: more than one embryo (citrus, mango) from nucellar cells

examples.title: Ploidy table
examples.problem: Give the ploidy of: nucellus, megaspore mother cell, functional megaspore, egg, endosperm, embryo.
examples.solution: Nucellus 2n, MMC 2n, megaspore n, egg n, endosperm 3n, embryo 2n.

examples.title: Embryo sac numbers
examples.problem: How many cells and nuclei are there in a typical embryo sac?
examples.solution: 7 cells (3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg, 1 central cell) and 8 nuclei (the central cell has 2 polar nuclei).

examples.title: Which prevents both?
examples.problem: Which device prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?
examples.solution: Dioecy (separate male and female plants), as in papaya.

examples.title: Fruit without seed
examples.problem: Banana fruits form without fertilisation. What is this called?
examples.solution: Parthenocarpy — fruit development without fertilisation (it can be induced with growth hormones).

examples.title: Pollen storage
examples.problem: How are pollen grains stored for crop breeding?
examples.solution: In liquid nitrogen at −196 °C (pollen banks), which keeps them viable for years.

examples.title: Synergid role
examples.problem: What is the function of the filiform apparatus?
examples.solution: It is a cellular thickening at the micropylar tip of synergids that guides the pollen tube into the synergid.

topics.title: Pre-fertilisation events
topics.explain: Hormonal and structural changes lead to differentiation of a floral primordium. An inflorescence bears floral buds; androecium and gynoecium differentiate.

topics.title: Pollen viability and allergy
topics.explain: Pollen of rice and wheat lose viability within 30 minutes; some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae keep it for months. Pollen of Parthenium (carrot grass) causes allergies and bronchial afflictions. Pollen tablets are used as food supplements.

topics.title: Pollen–pistil interaction
topics.explain: The pistil recognises compatible pollen and promotes germination; the pollen tube grows through the style and enters the ovule through the micropyle, then a synergid, releasing two male gametes. Artificial hybridisation uses emasculation (removing anthers) and bagging.

topics.title: Embryo development
topics.explain: The zygote divides after some endosperm forms. Dicot embryo: embryonal axis with two cotyledons, epicotyl (plumule) and hypocotyl (radicle). Monocot embryo: one cotyledon (scutellum), coleoptile around the shoot apex and coleorrhiza around the radicle.

topics.title: Seeds
topics.explain: Seeds are the final product of sexual reproduction; dormancy lets them survive bad conditions. Residual persistent nucellus is perisperm (black pepper, beet). Old seeds remain viable — lupine (~10,000 years), date palm (~2000 years).

topics.title: False fruits
topics.explain: In apple, strawberry and cashew the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation — these are false fruits. True fruits develop only from the ovary.

ratta: Apomixis: seed without fertilisation;  polyembryony: citrus, mango.
